idiom_name: circe generic-extras discriminator over a sealed trait ADT
implementation_notes: circe is the common JSON layer on Scala: model the messages as a sealed trait plus case classes and derive codecs with generic-extras, which - unlike the default derivation - can place an explicit discriminator field (Configuration.default.withDiscriminator("type") with deriveConfiguredDecoder). Default circe derivation for an ADT is untagged: it tries the constructors in order (alphabetically through circe-shapes), which is the inference the pattern exists to avoid. Scala 3's Mirror-based derivation and libraries such as jsoniter-scala or upickle offer the same explicitly tagged configuration, and the derived decoder enumerates the constructors, so no handwritten registry is needed while the hierarchy is sealed.
code_sketch:
sealed trait Event
final case class OrderCreated(id: String, total: Long) extends Event
final case class OrderCancelled(id: String, reason: String) extends Event

implicit val cfg: Configuration = Configuration.default.withDiscriminator("type")
implicit val decEvent: Decoder[Event] = deriveConfiguredDecoder   // tag -> case class
pitfalls: Default circe derivation is untagged: with overlapping case-class shapes the first constructor that decodes wins, so always configure a discriminator for wire formats.
withDiscriminator collides with a case class that already has a member of that name (a documented corner case), so keep the tag name out of the domain fields and define it once.
Tag values come from class names unless configured otherwise, so renaming a case class changes the wire tag for every consumer - pin the names with ConfiguredJsonCodec or an explicit mapping.
